title: A Sharded Change shares one Proposal and a Review per delivery batch
context: Each shard of a Migration was its own Change with its own slug and page, so following one migration meant reading several pages and the shard pages repeated the Migration's Proposal. The acceptance scenarios of the whole migration could not be checked at any single shard's G2.
decision: The shared-page model originally adopted for Migration applies to Sharded Change: one repository-owned specification and per-batch review history. WORKFLOW.md owns classification, branch/trailer rules, releasable boundaries and gates; this record retains why separate per-shard Change pages were rejected.

alternatives.option: Keep one Change page per shard
alternatives.reason: A reader pieces the migration together from several pages, and each shard page repeats the Proposal.

alternatives.option: Keep a slug per shard and list the shard pages on the Migration page
alternatives.reason: A mapping from shard slugs to their Migration would have to be maintained by hand.

alternatives.option: Let a scenario wait for a later shard without naming it
alternatives.reason: Which shard owes a scenario would stay unknown until the last G2.

consequences: The Migration commit trailer is no longer used; a shard is known by its branch suffix and its Shard trailer.
An ordinary Change keeps its unsuffixed branch and a single Review tab.
release-train generalizes the former Migration-only model; migrations remain a use case and do not maintain a separate delivery authority.
